quantiser_rule.decision: The CPU reference implements all three scale rules behind the optional `quant_rule` parameter of ernie_idx_query and ernie_idx_key; the default stays `nvidia` (the pinned model's per_token_group_quant_fp8) and is byte-identical to before. A device kernel must name the rule it implements and is judged against that rule's reference, never against another. For rocm_fnuz the CPU reference keeps OCP E4M3 code bytes, so parity is judged on the scale and on dequantised values (and downstream logits), not on raw cache code bytes. The rule that matches the shipped checkpoint on ROCm is decided by the first real-weights comparison (4-2 / epic 5), not by reading source.

rocm_fnuz.scale: 2^ceil(log2(max(amax, floor) / range)); exactly twice the rocm scale

quantiser_rule.effect: rows whose amax is at or below 448 * 2^-23 (about 5.3e-5) get the larger floor scale 2^-22 under rocm instead of a smaller one (so their codes lose resolution; rows between that and 1e-4 already get 2^-22 under nvidia); rocm_fnuz doubles every scale
quantiser_rule.not_emulated: the FNUZ e4m3 byte encoding (bias 8, no negative zero) is a device storage matter: the CPU reference keeps OCP E4M3 code bytes and only moves the scale and the code range

near_tie_fixture.decision: The tie rule of the indexer top-k (higher score first, lower index first on equal scores) is pinned at whole-model level, not only at op level (m06).
near_tie_fixture.fixture: tiny whole-model ERNIE checkpoint (the 3-6 geometry: dense and routed layers, MLA-DSA and HCA) with the indexer k_norm gamma and bias zeroed, so every key row is identical, every candidate score is exactly 0 and the tie rule alone chooses the attended tokens
near_tie_fixture.discrimination: the same prompt scored with the highest-index-first rule differs from the served result by more than 20x the 1e-4 tolerance

parity_band.decision: A device kernel is judged against the exact double-precision reference with a band that includes the rope-angle term, because a device kernel forms its rope angle from a float table.
parity_band.unit: relative to |q||k| of the rope slice (the bf16 storage term is also scaled by |q||k|, not by |reference|: it does not vanish when q.k is near zero; review of 4-1)

rope_angle_term_yarn_measured.note: the measured YaRN terms, carried explicitly: HCA p99 of |dot_f32table - dot_double| / (|q||k|) from rope-angle-precision.md

parity_band.rope_angle_term_note: rope_angle_term above is the band the checks enforce: the plain-theta p99 (2.8e-4 at 131k, 1.5e-3 at 1M) rounded up, which is >= the YaRN terms; the sealed test measures plain theta independently and requires the recorded term to be at or above it, so the measured YaRN values 2.3e-4 / 1.2e-3 alone would be too small for plain-theta rope layers. YaRN layers may use the tighter rope_angle_term_yarn_measured values
parity_band.source: the measured rope-angle precision (p99 of the f32 cos/sin table error; the terms are the plain-theta values rounded up, which bound the YaRN values too), re-measured by the 4-1 contract
